title: Vitruvyan Motus trace document, v1
description: DRAFT v1. A trace is a run header plus an ordered append-only sequence of records: the causal, replayable account of one run — what was read, decided, rejected, and caused, including time, randomness and generated identifiers. Canonical persisted forms: (a) a single JSON document matching this schema; (b) JSONL, where line 1 is `{"schema_version": ..., "run": <RunHeader>}` (this document minus `records`) and every further line is one Record validated against #/$defs/Record — so both forms name the schema version that produced them. Cross-record rules a conformant validator MUST enforce beyond this schema: (T1) `seq` is monotonic and gapless, starting at 1; (T2) the first record is kind=run_started; (T3) the last record of a finished run is run_completed | run_failed | run_cancelled — anything else is an in-flight or crash-truncated trace and MUST be treated as incomplete (guarantees.md invariant II); (T4) every `written_at` references the `seq` of an EARLIER transition record (or is null for initial-state keys, whose values are in run_started.initial_state); (T5) `node`, `after`, `selected` and `candidates[].target` name nodes declared in the fingerprinted GraphSpec, or the literal END where permitted; (T6) a transition aborted mid-flight by cancellation produces no transition record — run_cancelled is the next and last record, and the absence of the transition is itself the evidence. Integrity fields (payload/prev hashing) are RESERVED in v1.0: producers MUST emit `integrity` with null members; activation is a v1.x additive change. Conformant validators run with JSON Schema format assertion enabled (see contract/README.md).

schema_version.description: Version of THIS trace schema. Single-sourced in the package; a contract test asserts equality.

run_id.description: Exposed as `.trace_id` on the legacy compatibility view (guarantees.md §4).

spec_schema_version.description: The graphspec schema version the spec was validated against.

durability_profile.description: Which crash guarantee this run bought. See guarantees.md invariant II.

sink.description: Sink configuration disclosing the loss window. REQUIRED (validator rule) when durability_profile is `buffered`; optional otherwise.

replay.description: The capability DECLARED at run start. The FINAL capability — after any mid-run downgrade (node-protocol.md §6.2) — is on the terminal record; when both exist, the terminal record is authoritative.

metadata.description: Run provenance. Open map; these keys are documented and expected by tooling. Absorbs the run-metadata design merged post-0.4.0 (ADR-001 §dispositions).

actor.description: Whose authority the run acts under.

causation_id.description: The event that woke this run.

correlation_id.description: The broader request this run belongs to.

carta_version.description: Which rules were in force (consumer-defined constitution version).

capability.description: Explicit, recorded property. Absence of a declaration never implies reproducibility; a run that did not declare it is `none`. A node drawing ambient nondeterminism outside RunContext downgrades this to partial or none (invariant IV).

constraints.description: Machine-readable reasons for a non-full capability, e.g. 'node:fetch_page:ambient_time'.

ts.description: From the run clock — never from ambient wall time (invariant IV.1).

intent.description: The run's declared intent, if any.

initial_state.description: Snapshot of every fact present before the first transition (may be empty). Reads with written_at: null resolve here — without this, a seeded run is unreplayable and why-value-unanswerable for its seed keys.

node.description: Node name as declared in the GraphSpec (T5).

attempt.description: 1 for the first execution; retries increment. Every attempt gets its own transition record — retries are never hidden.

status.description: completed: the node returned. failed: the node raised and policy strict ends the run (a run_failed record follows, possibly after retries). skipped: the node raised under policy exploration — `error` is non-null and captured reads plus any writes that survive per the exploration contract are preserved; execution continues. A node that never started produces no record at all (T6).

effect_class.description: The node's resolved class (declared in the GraphSpec or defaulted to external_effect). Recorded here so the trace document is self-sufficient for replay-mode selection without resolving the spec.

key.description: The state key actually read (captured, not declared).

written_at.description: seq of the earlier transition that wrote the value read (T4), or null for initial-state keys (resolved in run_started.initial_state). This is the causal edge: why-value and first-divergence resolve through it.

writes.description: Everything this transition appended. A value is born inside the transition that wrote it — per-value provenance is structural, not reconstructed.

effects.description: Per-effect descriptions (node-protocol.md §4). v1.0 records description only; receipts and reuse-on-replay are a v1.x additive extension (0.6).

context_draws.description: Every RunContext draw this node made, in draw order. Empty for nodes that drew nothing. This is what makes invariant IV auditable and replay possible.

violations.description: Declared-vs-captured mismatches (node-protocol.md §3.2). Recorded in v1.0; enforcement is version-gated.

after.description: The node whose completion triggered this routing (T5).

on.description: The decision key routed on; null for a static next/terminal step.

value.description: The decision value observed; null for a static step.

written_at.description: seq of the transition that wrote the decision routed on (the routing record's own causal edge); null for a static step.

outcome.description: matched: value hit a map key. default: value missed and the route's default was taken. miss: value missed a strict route (graphspec R7) — selected is END, and the run then fails under policy strict or ends with the miss on record under exploration. static: a next/terminal step, no dispatch.

selected.description: A declared node name, or the literal string END.

target.description: A declared node name, or the literal string END.

candidates.description: Every route that was possible at this point, taken and not taken. The not-taken alternatives are first-class trace content — this is what why-not answers are made of.

replay.description: FINAL replay capability after any mid-run downgrade. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

failed_node.description: The node whose failure ended the run, when attributable. The accumulated trace up to and including this record survives — failure preservation is invariant-level (guarantees.md, inherited corpus).

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

reason.description: Cancellation is a first-class, trace-recorded runner outcome — never a silently abandoned generator. A node in flight at cancellation produces no transition record (T6).

replay.description: FINAL replay capability. Authoritative over the header's declared value.

source.description: Free-form provenance label supplied by the node. The kernel records it and never interprets it.

class.description: The class of THIS effect. `pure` is a node-level classification (see Transition.effect_class), not an effect — a pure effect is an oxymoron and does not validate.

idempotency_key.description: Required for external_effect once effect enforcement lands (0.7); optional and recorded-only in v1.0.

RedactedValue.description: Invariant V: structural completeness without content exposure. The hash and policy reference are evidence; the secret is not. NOTE: a plain-JSON object value whose own 'kind' field equals 'redacted' would be ambiguous; node-protocol.md §5 therefore forbids nodes from writing objects with a top-level 'kind': 'redacted' except through the redaction API.

Json.description: Any JSON value. Nodes may only write what can be written down — a value that cannot serialize is a contract violation at the boundary, not a silent pass-through.

Timestamp.description: RFC 3339, UTC, from the run clock (invariant IV.1).

Fingerprint.description: Kind-prefixed SHA-256 over canonical form. See contract/README.md.
